A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same shopping-behavior simulation study despite the changed title. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–B are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: V5 reports original model evaluations, reasoning ablations, action distributions, and error analyses using real shopping data, including the full results in appendix Table 2.

after.justification: V7 retains these original empirical results in Table 1, Figures 2–3, and appendix Table 3, and adds concrete prediction examples in Table 2.

M1.justification: Both versions use simplified HTML, hierarchical element names, three browser operations, Claude-generated reasoning, and fine-tuning with context-token losses masked. The reasoning-then-action generation procedure and Appendix A prompts are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both use the same online-shopping corpus: 31,865 sessions, 3,526 users, and 230,965 actions. Next-action generation and final purchase/termination prediction remain the evaluated tasks. The new consent description does not establish different population coverage.

E2.justification: Matching v5 appendix Table 2 against v7 appendix Table 3 establishes the same comparator membership. The additional baseline rows displayed in v7's main Table 1 were already evaluated and reported in v5's appendix.

E3.justification: Section 3.2 revises the described think-aloud demonstration source from one customer's sessions to customers' sessions, without specifying the new participant count. This is a limited reported sampling revision, not evidence of rerunning experiments. Evaluation procedures, metrics, and listed training hyperparameters otherwise match.

E4.justification: V7 adds two concrete search-refinement cases in Table 2: expanding 'disney gift' and correcting 'tee conector.' These expose Qwen2.5-7B and Claude predictions supporting v5's existing qualitative discussion. The reasoning ablation and aggregate error analysis remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both report the same McNemar tests and thresholds, p < 10^-10 and p < 10^-5. Neither supplies repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or additional uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: All 28 accuracy/F1 result pairs match between the full appendix tables. V7 adds prediction examples, a reported mean of 2.82 searches per session, and calculated comparison percentages. Its new Section 4.5 upper gain of 69.69% conflicts with Table 1's 69.39%.

T1.justification: The formal next-action mapping and task definitions are retained. Neither version contains theoretical propositions or proofs. V7's discussion of alternative evaluation principles introduces no formal metric or derivation.

C1.justification: The revised title, abstract, and three-item contribution list retain the central claims: quantitative process-centric shopping evaluation, poor prompt-only behavioral alignment, and improvements through fine-tuning and synthetic reasoning. The newly highlighted performance numbers were already reported in v5.

C2.justification: Section 3.2 replaces assurances that synthetic traces reflect human reasoning with an explicit predictive-aid interpretation that does not claim to reproduce actual thoughts. Section 5.1 adds substantive discussion of nondeterministic behavior and tolerating plausible action variants. The formal Limitations paragraph is unchanged.

D1.justification: V7 newly documents beta-user consent, anonymization, inability to release the dataset, local execution of open-source models, and approximately three hours per training job and 3,700 H200 GPU-hours overall. Conversely, it removes v5's disclosure of 357 test sessions and 932 test cases. Appendix prompts and example HTML are retained.

R1.justification: V7 adds Multi-Agent-as-Judge, AgentA/B, Sun et al.'s shopping-assistant evaluation, and Eccles and Arsal's think-aloud methodology reference, while removing Cao et al. These modestly broaden application context and methodological attribution without substantially changing research positioning.

P1.justification: V7 retitles the paper and substantially rewrites the abstract, introduction, ablation narrative, discussion, and future-work passages. The introduction is reorganized around multi-turn behavioral accuracy and the contributions are restructured, although the overall section sequence remains.

P2.justification: Both performance tables are extensively redesigned with category bands, colored comparison columns, and reordered rows; main Table 1 becomes full-width. Figure 1 is redrawn, the case-study Table 2 is added, and Figure 3's axis changes from 'Percentage' to 'Error Count.' Denser typesetting also substantially reflows the appendices.

improvement.justification: V7 more carefully explains the evidential role of synthetic reasoning and the ambiguity of matching human actions, while concrete prediction examples make its error-analysis claims easier to assess. Data-provenance and compute disclosures also improve transparency. These gains are partly offset by removing the test-set counts and introducing the 69.69%/69.39% inconsistency; the central experimental evidence is unchanged.
